parts.title: Section 3
parts.passageHtml:
{[Since 776 B. C. , when the Greek people held their first-ever Olympic Games, the Games were hosted every four years at the Olympia city.][317734]} {[Back then, a long journey for the Olympic torch was made before the opening ceremony of each Olympic Games.][317760]} {[The Greek people would light a cauldron of flames on the altar, a ritual devoted to Hera, the Greek Goddess of birth and marriage.][317779]}

{[The reintroduction of flame to the Olympics occurred at the Amsterdam 1928 Games, for which a cauldron was lit yet without a torch relay.][317803]} {[The 1936 Berlin Summer Games held the first Olympic torch relay, which was not resumed in the Winter Olympics until in 1952.][317825]} {[However, in that year the torch was lit not in Olympia, Greece, but in Norway, which was considered as the birthplace of skiing.][317848]} {[Until the Innsbruck 1964 Winter Olympics in Austria, the Olympic flame was reignited at Olympia.][317872]}

{[The torch is originally an abstract concept of a designer or groups of designers.][317889]} {[A couple of design groups hand in their drafts to the Olympic Committee in the hope that they would get the chance to create the torch.][317901]} {[The group that wins the competition will come up with a design for a torch that has both aesthetic and practical value.][317927]} {[After the torch is completed, it has to succeed in going through all sorts of severe weather conditions.][317948]} {[The appearance of the modem Olympic torch is attributed to a Disney artist John Hench, who designed the torch for the 1960 Winter Olympics in Squaw Valley, California.][317967]} {[His design laid a solid foundation for all the torches in the future.][317994]}

{[The long trip to the Olympic area is not completed by one single torch, but by thousands of them, so the torch has to be replicated many times.][318004]} {[Approximately 10,000 to 15,000 torches are built to fit thousands of runners who take the torches through every section of the Olympic relay.][318033]} {[Every single runner can choose to buy his or her torch as a treasurable souvenir when he or she finishes his or her part of the relay.][318055]}

{[The first torch in the modem Olympics (the 1936 Berlin Games) was made from a slender steel rod with a circular platform at the top and a circular hole in the middle to jet flames.][318080]}

{[The name of the runner was also inscribed on the platform as a token of thanks.][318113]} {[In the earlier days, torches used everything from gunpowder to olive oil as fuels.][318129]} {[Some torches adopted a combination of hexamine and naphthalene with a flammable fluid.][318144]} {[However, these materials weren’t exactly the ideal fuel sources, and they could be quite hazardous sometimes.][318156]} {[In the 1956 Olympics, the torch in the final relay was ignited by magnesium and aluminium, but some flaming pieces fell off and seared the runner’s arms.][318174]}

{[To promote the security rate, liquid fuels made its first appearance at the 1972 Munich Games.][318203]} {[Since then, torches have been using fuels which are pressurised into the form of a liquid.][318220]} {[When the fuels are burnt, they turn into gas to produce a flame.][318236]} {[Liquid fuel becomes safer for the runner and can be stored in a light container.][318249]} {[The torch at the 1996 Atlanta Summer Olympics is equipped with an aluminium base that accommodates a tiny fuel tank.][318264]} {[As the fuel ascends through the modified handle, it is squeezed through a brass valve that has thousands of little openings.][318283]} {[As the fuel passes through the tiny openings, it accumulates pressure.][318304]} {[Once it makes its way through the openings, the pressure decreases and the liquid becomes gas so it can bum up.][318315]}

{[The torch in 1996 was fuelled by propylene, a type of substance that could give out a bright flame.][318338]} {[However, since propylene was loaded with carbon, it would produce plenty of smoke which was detrimental to the environment.][318356]} {[In 2000, the designers of the Sydney Olympic torch proposed a lighter and cheaper design, which was harmless to the environment.][318376]} {[For the fuel, they decided to go with a combination of 35 per cent propane (a gas that is used for cooking and heating) and 65 per cent butane (a gas that is obtained from petroleum), thus creating a powerful flame without generating much smoke.][318397]}

{[Both the 1996 and 2000 torches adopted a double flame burning system, enabling the flames to stay lit even in severe weather conditions.][318427]} {[The exterior flame bums at a slower rate and at a lower temperature.][318450]} {[It can be perceived easily with its big orange flame, but it is unstable.][318462]} {[On the other hand, the interior flame bums faster and hotter, generating a small blue flame with great stability, due to the internal site offering protection of it from the wind.][318477]} {[Accordingly, the interior flame would serve as a pilot light, which could relight the external flame if it should go out.][318508]}

{[As for the torch of 2002 Olympics in Salt Lake City, the top section was made of glass in which the flame burned, for the purpose of echoing the theme of ‘Light the Fire Within’ of that Olympics.][318530]} {[This torch was of great significance for the following designs of the torches.][318569]}

questions.explanationHtml:
{[

severe weather conditions

“The Olympic torch, as requested by the Olympic Committee, will be carefully designed so that it is capable of withstanding all kinds of …………………..”: Ngọn đuốc Olympic - theo yêu cầu của ban tổ chức - sẽ được thiết kế sao cho có thể chịu được mọi loại ………….

Giải thích: Sau khi đuốc được hoàn thành, nó phải thành công trải qua đủ loại ĐIỀU KIỆN THỜI TIẾT KHẮC NGHIỆT (all sorts of SEVERE WEATHER CONDITIONS)

][1]}

{[

aesthetic and practical

“Generally, the design of the modern Olympic torch enjoys the ……………….. value.”: Thông thường thì ngọn đuốc Olympic hiện đại chứa đựng giá trị ………..

Giải thích: Nhóm thắng giải sẽ phải thiết kế một ngọn đuốc có giá trị THẨM MĨ lẫn THỰC TIỄN (AESTHETIC AND PRACTICAL value)

][2]}

{[

treasurable souvenir

“Each runner has an opportunity to purchase the torch as a(n) ……………”: mỗi người chạy sẽ có cơ hội mua ngọn đuốc như một ………….

Giải thích: mỗi người rước đuốc đều có thể mua lại ngọn đuốc của họ như một MÓN QUÁ LƯU NIỆM QUÝ BÁU (TREASURABLE SOUVENIR)

][3]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 4 - 9:

Look at the following statements and the list of Olympic torches below. Match each statement with the correct Olympic torch, A-H. 

Write the correct letter, A-H, in boxes 4-9 on your answer sheet.

List of Olympic Torches

A          ancient Greek Olympic flames
B          Berlin Games torch (1936)
C          1952 Winter Games flame
D          1956 Games torch
E          Munich Games torch (1972)
F          1996 torch (Atlanta)
G         2000 torch (Sydney)
H         2002 torch (Salt Lake City)

questions.explanationHtml:
E

“first liquid fuel”: nhiên liệu lỏng đầu tiên

Giải thích: Nhiên liệu lỏng xuất hiện lần đầu tiên (made its first appearance) ở Thế Vận Hội Munich năm 1972

F

“not environmentally friendly”: không thân thiện với môi trường

Giải thích: ngọn đuốc năm 1996 dùng nhiêu liệu là propylene. Nhưng vì propylene có rất nhiều carbon (loaded with carbon) → tạo ra rất nhiều khói (produce plenty of smoke) → có hại (detrimental) cho môi trường

questions.text: Beginning to record the runners’ name
questions.explanationHtml:
B

“beginning to record the runners’ name”: bắt đầu ghi nhận lại tên của người rước đuốc

Giải thích: Ngọn đuốc trong Thế Vận Hội Berlin (1936) có khắc tên những người rước đuốc (the name of the runner was also inscribed) để cảm ơn họ (as a token of thanks)

questions.text: Potentially risky as it burnt the runner’s arms
questions.explanationHtml:
D

“potentially risky as it burnt the runner’s arms”: nguy hiểm vì có thể làm bỏng tay người rước đuốc

Giải thích: trong Olympics năm 1956, một số mảnh bốc cháy (flaming pieces) rơi ra ngoài và làm cháy sém tay của người cầm đuốc (seared the runner’s arms)

H

special for a theme of ‘Light’: đặc biệt dành cho chủ đề “thắp sáng”

Giải thích: ngọn đuốc năm 2002 được làm bằng thủy tinh → phù hợp với chủ đề của thế vận hội này là “Light the Fire Within” (thắp sáng ngọn lửa bên trong)

C

“not lit in Greece”: không được thắp ở Hi Lạp

Giải thích: Vào “năm đó” (ở đây đang ám chỉ năm 1952), đuốc không thắp ở đỉnh Olympia ở Hi Lạp mà là ở Na Uy

questions.explanationHtml:
{[

double flame

“burner system of a ………….”:  hệ thống buồng đốt ………..

Giải thích: ngọn đuốc năm 1996 và 2000 đều sử dụng hệ thống đốt LỬA ĐÔI (a DOUBLE FLAME burning system)

][10]}

{[

propane and butane

“the liquid fuel mix of …………. stored in”: hỗn hợp nhiên liệu gồm ………. được trữ trong này

Giải thích: Bạn lưu ý đây là bản thiết kế đuốc của 1996 lẫn 2000 nhé, và vào năm 2000 nhiên liệu đã thay đổi rồi (vì vấn đề môi trường). Cây đuốc năm 2000 sử dụng kết hợp 35% propane và 65% butane.

][13]}

{[

openings

“a brass valve with many small ………….”: một cái van đồng với nhiều cái ………… nhỏ

Giải thích:  nhiên liệu len lỏi qua một cái van bằng đồng mà có hàng nghìn KHE HỞ nhỏ (has thousands of little OPENINGS).

][11]}

{[

handle

“pressurized fuel rises from the improved …………..”: nhiên liệu được nén lại bốc lên từ cái ………….. đã được cải tiến

Giải thích: mình phải đi ngược lại xíu để thấy được chi tiết “khi nhiên liệu bốc hơn lên” (as the fuel ascends) thông qua một cái TAY CẦM đã được chỉnh lại (through the modified HANDLE)

][12]}

{[

a fuel tank / tiny fuel tank / fuel tank

“………. coated by aluminum base”: được bọc bởi chân đế bằng nhôm

Giải thích: chân đuốc nhôm chứa một BÌNH ĐỰNG NHIÊN LIỆU NHỎ (accommodates a tiny fuel tank) → bạn cân nhắc chọn cho đủ 3 từ nhé: “a fuel tank”, “tiny fuel tank” hoặc “fuel tank”

][14]}
